Kim and team,

Thanks again for the demo last week — leadership asked us to lock down the cost picture before next Tuesday's board packet. Two quick asks so we can finalize the MAP: 1) a one-page tokens-per-dollar snapshot for the proposed config (we need an apples-to-apples metric across candidate models / quant levels), and 2) a short note on the caching & batching assumptions that went into that snapshot (hit rates you used, average batch sizes, latency SLO targets that would trigger smaller batches).

We also want to make sure the evaluation plan will stress the realistic traffic profile (bursty triage queues + steady daytime load). Can you confirm timelines so procurement can plan an SOW?

Alex — thanks, I pulled together the first-pass artifacts and attached them here: token-econ-snapshot.pdf (one-pager) and atlas_map_v2.xlsx (MAP draft with milestones & evaluation gates). High level answers below; Karthik added technical details in a separate note.

Quick summary:
- Tokens/$: snapshot includes three scenarios (hosted small model, hosted quantized medium, dedicated 8-GPU) with normalized tokens-per-dollar under your test profile. See the "Summary" tab in the spreadsheet.
- Caching assumptions: we used a 35% prefix-KV cache hit rate for intent routing flows and 10% for long-form assistant queries. We can parameterize that in the MAP if you want conditional gates.
- Batching: average batch size assumed = 4 requests per micro-batch during peak, and 1.5 off-peak. We modeled a latency SLO of 250ms p95 for the primary route; if you need stricter latency we reduce batching which increases cost (numbers in the snapshot).

Timeline for evaluation & SOW:
- Eval kickoff (traffic replay): 2026-11-09 through 11-20
- MAP gating review (tokens/$ signoff): 2026-11-23
- Procurement SOW ready to sign: 2026-11-30 (we can accelerate to 11-25 with a written confirmation of expected QPS)

Attaching: token-econ-snapshot.pdf, atlas_map_v2.xlsx.

On Thu, Nov 5, 2026 at 11:03 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Alex — thanks, I pulled together the first-pass artifacts and attached them here...

Adding the technical detail requested for the token-econ tracing in the snapshot so procurement and your engineering team have full visibility. Key points and how we modeled them:

1) Traffic & tokenization
- Avg tokens per user request (submission -> final): 120 tokens (baseline), 300 tokens for long-form flows. Snapshot weights these 2 classes at 80/20 unless you give us traffic distribution.

2) Caching model
- Prefix/KV cache hit rate assumption: 35% for quick intent responses (FAQ/lookup style), 10% for long-form.
- Cache eviction policy: LRU with 24-hour TTL on session prefixes for evaluation run.

3) Batching & latency tradeoffs
- Batch window: 8ms micro-batch accumulation we modeled for 250ms p95 SLO at 400 QPS
- Average per-GPU batch size in peak simulations: 4 — this is conservative; we flagged a sensitivity at batch size 2 which raises token cost ~12% in our sims.

4) Model variants & quantization impact
- We modeled three model tiers: small FP16, medium 8-bit quant, and a fallback distilled variant. Tokens-per-dollar in the snapshot are normalized to the small FP16 baseline. Quantized medium reduces cost per token by ~28% in throughput but increases tail latency for >1024 seqs — we show where that matters.

5) Failure / fallback policy
- Automatic degrade to the distilled fallback after 500ms generation timeout; cost impact is included as a blended rate in the snapshot.

6) Measurement plan during eval
- We'll capture real KV hit rates from your replay and update the MAP gating numbers after week 1. If observed hit rates are >=45% for prefix flows, tokens/$ improves by ~18% vs our baseline.

If you want a tighter latency bound (p95 <= 150ms) we can re-run sims but expect a ~20-30% increase in cost for the same throughput due to smaller batching.

Happy to hop on a short call with your infra team to walk the assumptions through — otherwise, we can parameterize them as variables in the MAP spreadsheet so procurement has a clear gating checklist.

—Karthik

- Procurement prefers the MAP include a short clause that we will re-run the tokens/$ after week 1 of the replay and allow a one-time adjustment to committed capacity if the delta is >10%. Can you add that gating checkbox to the MAP?
- We're comfortable with the fallback policy as specified; please document the 500ms degrade rule in the MAP appendix.

Procurement, can you confirm internal signoff process? procurement@atlashealth.com — if you can share the vendor intake form and target sign date (we're aiming 2026-11-30), we'll queue legal.

Kimberly — once you re-run the snapshot with 75/25 long-form weighting, send the updated one-pager and we will fold into the board packet Monday morning.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
